newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga delays drilling in Barents Sea.
newsitem.headline: Saga delays drilling in Barents Sea.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday it had postponed plans to spud a well in the Barents Sea until next August.
The company had planned to drill well 7219/8-2 this winter but decided to delay the project after consultation with Den norske stats oljeselskap.
The Transocean Arctic rig, which was scheduled to do the drilling, has been delayed off mid-Norway, Saga said in its weekly newsletter.
"Saga originally planned to drill the well in cooperation with Statoil to optimise mobilisation, emergency response and base cost for Transocean Arctic," the company said.
Saga's and Statoil's wells were due to be completed before the award of new licences, expected in April.
"Strategically, results from Statoil's 7228/7-11 well in the North Cape are more important for Saga's application for new licences in this area than the outcome of its own well," Saga said.
Licence terms for the area related to environmental considerations restrict drilling by Saga from March 20 to August 1.
